01 — Case Files

Every project starts as a hypothesis

Two academic studies, run the way a statistician runs them: state H₀, pick a test, let the data argue.

CASE 01 · Applied Regression Analysis
What actually drives a diamond's price?
REJECT H₀

A multiple linear regression study over a 53,940-record Kaggle diamond dataset (carat, cut, colour, clarity, depth, table, and physical dimensions) to quantify what really moves price — and to catch the classic trap of correlated predictors before believing the coefficients. View report + R code on GitHub ↗

H₀ — NULL
None of carat, cut, colour, clarity, depth, table or dimensions affect diamond price.
H₁ — ALTERNATIVE
At least one variable significantly affects price.
  • Built a multiple linear regression model with price as the dependent variable.
  • Diagnosed multicollinearity with Variance Inflation Factor — carat, x, y and z turned out to be measuring almost the same thing (VIF as high as 130).
  • Applied a log transform to price to fix skew and stabilize variance.
  • Interpreted results as % price change per unit rather than raw dollars, post-transform.
Dataset size53,940 rows
R² (original model)0.856
R² (log-transformed)0.900
F-statistic p-value< 2.2e-16
Max VIF (carat/x/y/z)129.9
Multiple Linear Regression R VIF Diagnostics Log Transformation
CASE 02 · Survey & Non-Parametric Testing
Do listening habits split by gender or genre?
FAIL TO REJECT H₀

A primary-data survey of 68 respondents on music consumption — from designing a simple random sampling plan through three non-parametric tests to a Power BI dashboard, run to check whether the visible patterns actually held up statistically. View report + R code on GitHub ↗

H₀ — NULL
No significant difference between the variables being compared (gender vs. genre, platform vs. platform, genre vs. genre).
H₁ — ALTERNATIVE
A significant difference exists between the variables.
  • Designed a simple random sampling plan and collected primary data from 68 respondents.
  • Ran a Chi-Square test of independence on gender × genre preference.
  • Ran a Kruskal–Wallis H test comparing Pop, Hip-Hop and Classical listenership.
  • Ran a Mann–Whitney U test comparing Spotify vs. YouTube Music usage.
  • Built a Power BI dashboard to visualize the descriptive-layer findings.
Respondents surveyed68
Preferred genre — Pop44%
Preferred platform — Spotify63%
Chi-Square (gender × genre)p = 0.255
Chi-Square Test Kruskal–Wallis Mann–Whitney U Power BI R
